edge: Process bootstrap files with zero comments and with consecutive comments between entries.
positive: Process a bootstrap file with multiple comment lines between two library entries and observe both entries being honored.

edge: Use both an unindented comment and a comment preceded by several blanks.
negative: Use a line with nonblank text before #; it does not satisfy the bootstrap comment-line syntax.
positive: Use a newline-terminated bootstrap comment whose first nonblank character is #.

edge: Use an extensionless relative pathname containing directory components.
negative: Put the platform-specific shared-library extension in the bootstrap entry pathname; the line does not satisfy the defined entry syntax.
notes: The concrete direct-library option spelling is implementation-defined; equivalence is to that facility's pathname value.
positive: Place an extensionless library pathname as the only nonblank content of a bootstrap entry and observe the corresponding platform shared library being integrated.

edge: Use a bootstrap file with no library entries after its required first line.
negative: Put two library locations on one entry line; the line does not satisfy the one-entry-per-line syntax.
positive: Use two bootstrap entry lines, each holding one distinct library location, and observe both entries being processed.

edge: Use exactly one leading blank and no trailing blanks.
negative: Use an otherwise valid library entry beginning in the first column with no preceding blank.
positive: Use a bootstrap entry with one leading blank and another with multiple leading and trailing blanks; both satisfy the whitespace grammar.

edge: Specify the bootstrap file by a relative pathname and combine this rule with the Annex J root-resolution rules.
notes: Concrete command-line switch spelling is advisory under J.2; use the implementation's corresponding facility.
positive: Identify one bootstrap file containing an object-code entry through the bootstrap-file pathname facility and invoke its DPI routine.

edge: Place the required string exactly on the first line before entries.
negative: Use a bootstrap file whose first line omits or misspells #!SV_LIBRARIES.
positive: Load a bootstrap file beginning with #!SV_LIBRARIES.

edge: Refer to the same file through hard-linked pathnames detectable as identical.
positive: Specify the identical library through both a bootstrap file and direct library facility and observe bootstrap precedence.

edge: Interleave multiple bootstrap-file and direct-library specifications in one invocation.
positive: In one invocation, load one DPI library via a bootstrap file and another via direct library specification, then call both.

edge: Place a relative file reference before a later root-directory option and resolve that earlier reference from the working directory.
notes: Materialization needs control of simulator working directory and command-line ordering.
positive: From a chosen working directory, load a relative-path DPI artifact without supplying a root-directory switch.

edge: Use separate direct-library instances for two extensionless library basenames.
negative: Pass the platform-specific shared-library extension as part of the direct library pathname.
positive: Specify a directly loaded shared library by pathname basename without its platform extension.

edge: Run the same basename convention on platforms with differing shared-library extensions.
positive: Provide an extensionless direct-library basename whose platform-specific shared library exists and invoke a DPI routine from it.

edge: Use precompiled target-platform object code rather than compiling its foreign-language source as part of the simulation invocation.
notes: Materialization requires a target-platform object artifact and a portable build/load harness.
positive: Supply a target-platform shared library implementing a DPI-imported routine through an Annex J inclusion method and invoke it from SystemVerilog.

edge: Refer to one library through both identical and filesystem-aliased pathnames and observe a single load when the files are identifiable as the same.
notes: The oracle must observe library loading or registration, not merely repeated calls to an exported DPI routine.
positive: Specify the same library multiple times and use an observable registration counter to verify that its load-time registration occurs once.

edge: Use multiple entries in each method and observe the transition from the final bootstrap entry to the first direct specification.
notes: Materialization requires a portable observable registration mechanism and must not rely on diagnostic wording.
positive: Use observable registration effects to verify bootstrap libraries load in entry-line order before directly specified libraries load in occurrence order.

edge: Use two bootstrap files that each name a distinct library to make processing of both files observable.
notes: The concrete command-line switch spelling is implementation-defined; Annex J standardizes the facility's behavior, not its option name.
positive: Specify two bootstrap files through repeated uses of the bootstrap-file location facility and observe libraries from both files being processed.

edge: Place one required DPI entry point in each of two libraries so successful integration requires both facility occurrences.
notes: The concrete command-line switch spelling is implementation-defined; Annex J standardizes the facility's behavior, not its option name.
positive: Specify two distinct object-code libraries through repeated uses of the direct-library facility and observe imported DPI functionality from both.

edge: Use an absolute bootstrap-file location while a root directory is configured and verify that the absolute location is not formed as a root-relative path.
notes: Concrete option spellings are implementation-defined; exercise the corresponding Annex J location facilities. Relative pathname resolution is scored separately under J.3.
positive: Integrate one library using an absolute location and another using a relative location, using the two Annex J inclusion methods.

edge: Build the same fixture on two target platforms using each platform's corresponding shared-library extension.
negative: Name the supplied shared library with an extension for a different platform; it does not satisfy the required artifact naming condition.
notes: Requires a platform-aware fixture-building harness; no particular extension string is portable across platforms.
positive: Supply an Annex J shared library using the target platform's native shared-library filename extension.

edge: Use a minimal shared library exporting exactly one DPI routine.
negative: Supply a standalone unlinked object file where Annex J requires a shared library.
positive: Supply a target-platform shared library containing a DPI routine and load it through an Annex J method.

edge: Include an unrelated unreferenced function with a conflicting external symbol and verify its presence does not require loading that function.
notes: Materialization must distinguish loading selected object code from loading the shared-library image itself.
positive: Load a shared library where the DPI-imported function is referenced and invoke it.

edge: Use an absolute artifact path while a root directory is configured and verify that the absolute path is not prefixed.
notes: The facility's command-line spelling is recommended rather than mandatory; exercise the implementation's corresponding root-directory facility.
positive: Configure an Annex J root directory and load an artifact named by a relative path beneath it.
